items: A Settings window of its own, opened with the gear in the panel or Settings… in the menu-bar menu.
Give any external display its own brighter and dimmer shortcut, so you can change one without choosing it first.
Those keys can move every display, as before, or just the display you select.
If macOS has not allowed Accessibility, the setting says so and opens the exact pane in one click.
Save the settings your monitors report as a preset — Evening, Day, whatever you name it — and put them back with one click.
A preset only writes to the display it was saved from: a monitor that is no longer connected is reported, never swapped for another.
Fixes the update check giving up before it starts: the bundled framework could not read the token path when it began with ~.
Same app as 0.1.9 — the first release it installs by itself. From here, updates arrive without anyone installing a new copy.
Fixes the app quitting a second after launch: our own bundled update framework is now allowed to load, and the release checks that inside the shipped app.
The release gate now starts the app it built and fails if it does not survive.
The app can update itself: it checks its own signed feed, asks the app for a quiet moment first, and installs without a window or a prompt.
This build is the update pilot's baseline — installing it is the last hand install.
The app asks for the Accessibility permission it needs, instead of leaving the brightness keys doing nothing.
The panel drops from the menu-bar icon like a menu, with everything visible and no scrolling.
Same app as 0.1.5, repackaged so the release page can keep both the current and the previous download.
The app package no longer contains local build paths.
The panel now drops from the menu-bar icon like a menu, instead of floating as a window, and closes when you click elsewhere.
Everything fits the panel: no scrolling, no cut-off controls.
When F1/F2 cannot work yet, the panel shows the fix and its Open System Settings button up top, not a footnote.
The update hold now has its own port, so an update can never pause another app by mistake.
Only one copy can run: launching it again opens the panel instead of adding a second menu-bar icon.
Use the Mac's own F1/F2 brightness keys for external displays, once you allow Accessibility.
Move every display together with one slider.
Start automatically when you log in, with a switch in the panel.
A first-run explanation says what the app does and what to do when a monitor does not answer.
A setting the monitor does not report now says "Not reported" instead of showing 0.
Change the brightness of compatible external monitors from the menu bar.
Adjust contrast and monitor volume where the monitor reports those controls.
Make your displays brighter or dimmer with a keyboard shortcut, even when the panel is closed.
